claims.claim: Pydantic v2's model_copy(update=...) creates a copied model without validating the supplied update values.

newer_practice.summary: Pydantic 2.14.0a1 changes deep-copy handling so fields replaced by updates need not be deep-copied. This is a copying optimization, not update validation, and does not require changing this step.

claims.recommended_action: No factual correction required. Preserve the distinction between copying trusted values and validating new input; model_copy must not be described as a validation boundary.

sources.quote: The model_copy() method allows models to be duplicated (with optional updates that aren’t validated)
sources.title: Models — Pydantic Documentation, Model copy

claims.claim: SQLite permits one simultaneous write transaction, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE requests a write transaction immediately and may fail with SQLITE_BUSY when another writer is active.

newer_practice.summary: SQLite 3.50.0 introduces sqlite3_setlk_timeout for blocking-lock builds, separately from the busy timeout. This optional mechanism does not change single-writer semantics or eliminate possible BEGIN IMMEDIATE contention; no step change is required.

claims.recommended_action: No factual correction required. Retain BEGIN IMMEDIATE semantics and the explicit possibility of SQLITE_BUSY; successful transaction acquisition must not be assumed.

sources.quote: “only one simultaneous write transaction”; “BEGIN IMMEDIATE might fail with SQLITE_BUSY”
sources.title: SQLite — Transaction

claims.claim: A SQLite trigger can terminate an UPDATE or DELETE statement with RAISE(ABORT, message), returning a constraint error.
claims.recommended_action: No change required to the stated trigger mechanism. ABORT terminates the offending statement; it must not be interpreted as automatically rolling back every earlier statement in the surrounding transaction. No superseding practice affecting this claim was found.

sources.quote: RAISE(ABORT,...) … the current query terminates. An error code of SQLITE_CONSTRAINT …
sources.title: SQLite — CREATE TRIGGER, The RAISE() function

claims.claim: Python 3.12's standard-library hashlib provides a guaranteed sha256 constructor and hexadecimal digest output.
claims.recommended_action: No change required. sha256 and hexdigest support the claimed operation. Current Python 3.14 documentation retains these guarantees; no relevant replacement or superseding practice was found.

sources.quote: “always present in this module … sha256()”; “containing only hexadecimal digits”
sources.title: hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests — Python 3.12 Documentation

claims.claim: RFC 8785 canonical JSON sorts object property names by UTF-16 code units and encodes the resulting serialization as UTF-8.
claims.recommended_action: No factual correction required. Preserve UTF-16 code-unit ordering and UTF-8 output wherever RFC 8785 compatibility is claimed. The opened errata do not change either rule; no superseding practice was found in the search window.

sources.quote: “arrays of UTF-16 … code units”; “MUST be encoded in UTF-8.”
sources.title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS), Sections 3.2.3–3.2.4

claims.claim: A CLI-only access log and local seal/plan/registration timestamps cannot establish the absence of earlier external viewing or that generation occurred after sealing.

newer_practice.summary: C2PA 2.2 adds claimed signature creation time and updates timestamp handling and validation. This reinforces distinguishing recorded assertions from independently supported temporal evidence. It does not establish unseen access history or require expanding this locally bounded step.

claims.recommended_action: No change required: the claim already states the appropriate limitation. This conclusion is an inference from logging coverage and timestamp semantics: unobserved external viewing remains unknown, and later registration can describe an already-existing asset.

sources.quote: Applications vary significantly in the types of information that they log.
sources.title: NIST SP 800-92: Guide to Computer Security Log Management

sources.quote: A time-stamping service supports assertions of proof that a datum existed before a particular time.
sources.title: RFC 3161: Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP)

claims.claim: Pydantic model_copy(update=...) does not validate supplied update values; verify applicability to the locked Pydantic 2.13.5 version.

newer_practice.summary: The 2.14.0a1 prerelease documents an optimization for deep-copying updated models, not validation of update values. It does not change the verified 2.13.5 behavior or justify a dependency upgrade for this claim.

claims.recommended_action: No factual correction required: the version-tagged source explicitly confirms applicability to 2.13.5. The repository's actual lockfile and persistence call site were not independently inspected, so this finding alone does not establish an additional implementation defect.

sources.quote: Note: the data is not validated before creating the new model. You should trust this data.
sources.title: Pydantic v2.13.5 — BaseModel.model_copy source and API docstring

claims.claim: SQLite permits one simultaneous write transaction, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE requests that transaction immediately and can fail with SQLITE_BUSY.

newer_practice.summary: SQLite 3.50.0 adds a separate blocking-lock timeout interface for supported builds. This supplements contention handling without changing the claim or requiring integration into this step.

claims.recommended_action: No change required to the evaluator statement. The documentation confirms both immediate write acquisition and possible contention failure.

sources.quote: “only one simultaneous write transaction”; “BEGIN IMMEDIATE might fail with SQLITE_BUSY”
sources.title: SQLite — Transaction

claims.claim: SQLite triggers using RAISE(ABORT, message) terminate UPDATE or DELETE statements with a constraint error.
claims.recommended_action: No change required. The evaluator correctly identifies statement termination and the constraint error. No relevant superseding trigger behavior was found.

sources.quote: RAISE(ABORT,...) … the current query terminates. An error code of SQLITE_CONSTRAINT …
sources.title: SQLite — CREATE TRIGGER, The RAISE() function

claims.claim: Python 3.12 hashlib guarantees a sha256 constructor and hexadecimal digest output.
claims.recommended_action: No change required to the evaluator statement. Python 3.12 explicitly provides both capabilities, and newer documentation does not supersede these guarantees.

sources.title: hashlib — Secure hashes and message digests — Python 3.12 Documentation

claims.claim: RFC 8785 sorts object property names by UTF-16 code units and encodes the resulting serialization as UTF-8.
claims.recommended_action: No factual correction required. The evaluator accurately states the RFC's sorting and encoding rules. Neither the opened errata nor the recent-practice search identified a change to these requirements.

sources.quote: “arrays of UTF-16 … code units”; “MUST be encoded in UTF-8.”
sources.title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS), Sections 3.2.3–3.2.4

claims.claim: The locked Pydantic JsonValue validator rejects tuples produced by CheckedValue.unpack instead of accepting them as JSON arrays; confirm this dependency behavior underlying L04-R1-F01.
claims.recommended_action: Address L04-R1-F01 before integration: recursively convert unpacked array tuples to lists at the JsonValue boundary, preserving nested objects, array order, and scalar values. Add a regression covering the reported CheckedValue-to-generation path with nested and empty arrays. The tagged implementation dispatches Python tuples to an unmatched tuple tag, supporting rejection; the local producer and reproduction remain supplied premises, not independently inspected facts. No newer tuple-accepting JsonValue behavior was found.

sources.quote: “_JSON_TYPES = {int, float, str, bool, list, dict, type(None)}”; “custom_error_type='invalid-json-value'”
sources.title: Pydantic v2.13.5 — JsonValue and its type discriminator

proposals.rationale: The version-tagged dependency source confirms the rejection underlying L04-R1-F01. Normalize tuples recursively at the reported boundary and verify nested and empty array cases so valid JSON-array content can reach generation.
proposals.title: Normalize unpacked arrays before JsonValue validation

summary: Verified all 12 requested claims against opened primary sources. The ledger excerpt was empty. Searched for relevant developments from 2025-04-09 through 2026-10-09; none supersedes the claims. R0008-C012 requires action because the confirmed dependency behavior breaks the reported tuple-producing path. Its local reproduction and lockfile were not inspected under the file restriction. R0008-C006 is a supported inference about evidence limits. No landscape scan was required.
